engagement_title: Lanternwood Folk Fest 2027 on sale kit: rebuild the performer laminate run off last year's printed pass, recover the festival mark from the painted banner, and carry both onto the headliner posters and the lineup announcement
vertical: Party, Events and Promotion: an independent three stage folk and roots music festival held on a farm outside Burlington, Vermont, sixth edition, roughly four thousand weekend tickets
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork event credential post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, an events team wanting personalised backstage and performer passes produced from a lineup list against a designer built page layout template, delivered both as one file the printer can run and as separate passes to send out. Co anchor: the second Upwork post in the ledger, whose literal ask was to BUILD a page layout plugin that automatically reduces font sizes when a record is too long for its frame, because merged text runs overset and get clipped on export. That second post is a software commission and is out of scope for any design connector, but the PAIN it names is real, it is the single most common failure of a variable data print run, and this engagement makes the agent meet it by hand rather than automate it away. Both real posts name a client nowhere, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional festival Lanternwood Folk Fest; every performer, crew member, stage and sponsor name is invented and no real festival, venue, act or trademark appears in any task facing field. The ledger's repositioning note killed the original because it merged into a convert_pdf_to_indd output and relied on a per row data merge image field that cannot exist in a converted PDF. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: the convert, prepare, merge chain IS verified to bind fields end to end off a bare press PDF, provided the mapping offsets are computed from the true interchange story rather than from the tool's own readout, while the per row image field genuinely does not exist unless the source PDF carried a real placed image. So the corrected commission keeps the client's actual pass run and makes both of those realities load bearing, and it adds the rest of the kit that client obviously needed at the same on sale date.
client_one_liner: Twenty two people need laminates the printer can run, our designer left in 2024 and took the logo files, and on sale is the first Monday in February.
client_brief:
Lanternwood Folk Fest 2027, on sale kit

We run a three stage folk and roots festival on a farm outside Burlington. Sixth year. Weekend general admission is a hundred and forty five dollars, VIP is three hundred and twenty, and we sell about four thousand weekend tickets to a crowd between eighteen and forty who come as much for the discovery stages as for the headliners.

On sale is the first Monday in February and everything a ticket buyer or a performer sees has to be ready together.

Passes first, because the printer needs them earliest. Every performer, crew member and volunteer wears a laminate on a lanyard. Last year's pass is attached exactly as our printer returned it, and this year's is the same shape in our new colours. There are twenty two people on the roster and each needs their own pass carrying their name, their act, their role, the stages they are cleared for and the days they are on site. Roles are colour coded so gate staff can read them from two metres away. We need one file the printer can run in a single pass, and separate single passes we can email out to the acts.

Posters next. Three A2 directions for the headline nights, because we want to choose between them rather than be handed one. Then the lineup announcement set for social, a square, a tall one and a four by five, all in one working file, because acts move and we will be changing it ourselves through the winter.

The festival mark. Our designer left in 2024 and took the files with him. All that survives is a photograph of the painted banner that hangs over the main stage. We need the mark back as artwork we can put on the posters, the announcement set and the programme.

The photography is last year's, shot by two volunteers on two cameras across three stages. It does not read as one festival yet.

We also want the site plan drawn properly instead of the pencil scan, and one page recording our colours, our type and our mark so the next person does not have to do this again.
price_band_and_audience: Mid tier independent festival. Weekend general admission a hundred and forty five dollars, VIP three hundred and twenty, roughly four thousand weekend tickets, audience eighteen to forty, discovery led and scene literate rather than corporate. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push sparse and luxurious, with acres of white, a hairline serif and one small photograph, and it reads as a three hundred and twenty dollar tasting event rather than a farm field weekend, which suppresses general admission conversion where nearly all the revenue sits. Push the other way into a dense bargain flyer, with every act at the same size, a starburst price and clip art, and the VIP tier stops being credible and the discovery stages read as filler. The correct register is energetic and coherent: bold type at a real hierarchy, atmospheric photography carrying the field and the night, a lineup that plainly distinguishes headline from discovery, and colour coding a gate steward reads at two metres in daylight. A posted commission of this shape and scope runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Three stages, one field, after dark.
brand_identity.sector: An independent three stage folk and roots music festival held on a farm outside Burlington, sixth edition.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022, a farm outside Burlington, Vermont, a small core team programming roughly four thousand weekend tickets.
brand_identity.about: Lanternwood is an independent folk and roots festival on a farm outside Burlington, now in its sixth year. Three stages, a weekend under the lights, and a bill that gives its discovery acts the same care as its headliners. People come as much for the acts they have not heard of yet as for the ones on the poster, and the whole thing runs on that promise.
brand_identity.audience: A discovery led crowd aged eighteen to forty, scene literate rather than corporate, who buy on atmosphere and word of mouth and expect the field weekend to feel real rather than packaged.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Weekend general admission 145 dollars, VIP 320, roughly four thousand weekend tickets. Mid tier independent: energetic and coherent, a credible VIP tier without tipping into either luxury restraint or bargain flyer chaos.
brand_identity.typography: A bold condensed display face for the lineup and the headline nights, carrying a real hierarchy that separates headline from discovery at a glance, paired with a sturdy grotesque for body, set times and the site plan legend. The feel is poster energy, warm and a little rough, never polished.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, a bit of grit. It talks up the discovery stages as loudly as the headliners and keeps sponsor and billing lines exactly as agreed. Example line the brand would write: "Gates at five. Three stages till late. Come early for the names you will be bragging about next year."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our designer left in 2024 and took the logo files. The mark now survives only as a photograph of the painted canvas banner that has hung over the main stage since 2022. There is no vector, no source file and no written type or colour spec. Last year's photography was shot by two volunteers on two cameras with no brief.
brand_identity.values: Give the discovery acts the poster space, and keep the weekend feeling like a field rather than a brand.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_pass_2026.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's performer laminate artwork, the press PDF the printer returned, portrait, one pass per page, with a photo box, a name block, an act line, a role bar and a stage and day strip.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's pass, exactly as the printer sent it back. Same shape this year, new colours, new names."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The five blocks that read as separate fields on the printed page are one continuous text flow once converted, so there is nothing to map field by field, and the readout used to build a mapping silently omits the low contrast handle run while keeping its line break, which leaves every offset past it short by exactly that run while the validator still answers VALID and the prepare step still answers completed successfully. The photo box is drawn artwork rather than a placed image, so no graphic frame exists for a per performer headshot to bind to, and nothing in the printed page or the file listing says so.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_roster_2027.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twenty two rows: person, act, role, stages cleared, days on site, social handle, and a column of headshot filenames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everyone who wears a laminate. It is final apart from one crew name we are still confirming."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Several act strings run long (a duo billed with a guest brass section, one act carrying a parenthetical subtitle) and the pass measure does not overset visibly, it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the merge succeeds, the page count still equals the row count and the record reads as complete until the trim is examined. Role values arrive in three different spellings and cases across the twenty two rows, and the colour coding the client wants is keyed to them.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_banner_mainstage.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the painted canvas banner over the main stage, carrying the festival mark: a lantern with cut window panes, sitting inside a ring of small caps type, over a hand painted rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still exists since the drive went. It has hung there since 2022."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The trace comes back clean and convincing at canvas size, but the lantern's window panes and the counters inside the ring close up at the size the mark actually reproduces in the announcement set corner lockup and the site plan legend, on the dark ground those two sit on, and nothing reports it because the trace itself succeeded. The banner's right third hangs in shade where the painted ink and the canvas run close in value, so a selection worded for the ink alone comes back short on that side.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_stage_frames/ (14 frames, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's performance photography, shot by two volunteers on two different bodies across the three stages, mixed daylight, dusk and stage light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we have from last year. Some of it is lovely. It was two people with two cameras and no brief."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the fourteen are the same act photographed on the same night from three positions, and one of the three 2027 headliners appears in none of the fourteen at all, which no filename, caption or column reveals and which only surfaces when the frames are read against the billing. Two frames were shot into the low sun and sit a full stop hotter than the rest of the set.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_lineup_2027.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Approved billing: headline and discovery acts per stage per day, set times, the ticket tiers, the on sale date and the two sponsor lines that must appear.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The billing as approved. The sponsor lines are contractual and cannot be reworded."

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_site_plan_pencil.png
assets_supplied.kind: Scan of the site manager's hand drawn plan: three stages, the gates, the food row, camping, first aid and the accessible route.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How the field is laid out. Somebody needs to draw this properly."

acceptance_bar: Twenty two passes exist, one person per page, the page count equals the roster count, and every field on every pass carries that person's own value with nothing left inherited from last year's artwork.
No pass truncates. Every act string, every role and every stage and day list is present in full at trim on the delivered artwork, not merely accepted by the merge.
Separate single passes exist, one per person, named to the roster, and each one holds the right person.
Proofs are at true print resolution and sized to the pass trim, not a screen scale preview standing in for a proof.
Role colour coding is one scheme, legible from two metres in daylight, with the roster's inconsistent role spellings reconciled rather than passed through.

The festival mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it still reads as our mark at the smallest place it appears and on our darkest ground.
Three A2 poster directions sit in one working file and are genuinely three directions, not one layout in three colourways.
The announcement set is one working file carrying the square, the tall and the four by five, each keeping its own canvas size, with text we can retype and the mark as real vector shapes.
Every photograph in every delivered layout is actually present, on every canvas and not only the first one.

The fourteen stage frames read as one festival when laid together: one white point, one black point, one crop logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
Every act billed on a poster is represented by a photograph that is actually of that act, and no photograph stands in for two.
One type system across posters, announcement set, site plan and basis page, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
Anything that could not be produced is named plainly in the note rather than approximated silently.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (mapping and validation passes), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange All and per record), document_render_layout (createSeparateFiles, resolution)
adobe_surfaces.role: The entire laminate run, built backwards out of a bare press PDF because the client has no native file. This surface carries the reverse engineering of last year's artwork into a live merge template, the twenty two record run as one press file with one person per page, the per record single passes named to the roster, and the true resolution proofs. It is also where the two hardest realities of the commission live: what the conversion actually exposes as addressable frames, and whether a mapping the validator blessed actually landed.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Bringing fourteen frames shot by two volunteers on two bodies to one festival look, one frame at a time toward a single target rather than one batched move across a mixed set, plus the confined corrections the two into the sun frames need. It is also the whole of the mark recovery: an ink level selection off a photographed painted banner, the polarity decision before tracing, the bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, and the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for anyone.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express, asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: Everything the client will edit themselves: three A2 poster directions in one document, the mixed canvas announcement set, the site plan drawn as inline SVG so it stays editable vector, and the basis page. This is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout at all. Every photograph must be pulled down and carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored top and left, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system across the posters, the announcement set, the site plan and the basis page. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on a hundred and forty five dollar farm field weekend rather than on either a luxury or a bargain register. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, one unlaundered name kills the entire kit call, and the CSS must carry the returned slug or the face falls back with no error anywhere.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, orientation never passed), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one thing the archive does not contain, a field and dusk crowd atmosphere frame for the poster direction that needs it, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the selects the festival's two directors sign the poster direction off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial rather than as a failure.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The pass run is a record per page variable data job and belongs on the layout and merge surface; the posters, the announcement set, the site plan and the basis page are free form fixed canvases and can only be authored. The brief already pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset and hold each returned address against its role in a manifest.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handover discipline, and it matters more than usual here because the same roster file is consumed twice, once as merge data and once as billing to read the photography against.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of upload addresses keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Convert last year's pass PDF into an editable layout document, then export its interchange form and read what the document actually contains: how many text frames, what bounds, what typography, what graphic frames if any.
trajectory.judgement: The printed page is not evidence of structure. Frame granularity out of a PDF is not under anyone's control, and the only honest way to justify a mapping is to look at the converted document rather than at the artwork.
trajectory.produces: A converted layout document plus a frame inventory taken from its interchange form.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story text by concatenating the content runs from the interchange file, compute every mapping offset from that reconstructed string, and build the mapping against integer frame identifiers.
trajectory.judgement: The readout the mapping tool hands back is a convenience, not the document. Offsets computed from anything other than the true story are wrong in a way nothing downstream complains about.
trajectory.produces: A mapping built on reconstructed offsets, with the reconstruction retained for the note.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then verify it by exporting the interchange form again and confirming that every expected field placeholder is actually present in the story.
trajectory.judgement: Completed successfully is a status, not a verification. The only thing that proves a placeholder landed is finding it in the document afterwards.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been read back and reconciled field by field.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen stage frames and triage them against the approved billing: which volunteer and which body, which sit hot, which stage, and crucially which act each frame actually shows.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes the archive covers the festival. Counting files is not reading them, and only the billing can settle whether fourteen frames means fourteen usable subjects.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, exposure and subject identity against the billing.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, then fix one festival target from the most workable frame and correct each of the fourteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels so it cannot follow a crop. The target is a set, not fourteen good pictures: one batched move applies one identical correction, which is exactly wrong across two bodies and three lighting situations.
trajectory.produces: Graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Apply confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate: naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate. The two into the sun frames need the sky held back without taking the crowd with it.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the field yellow or the stage flat.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the banner: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, the correct polarity before tracing, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the paint and not the canvas, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or a colour accurate plate is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring entirely.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole kit of work.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a hundred and forty five dollar weekend ticket and a discovery led crowd. A weight cannot be inferred from a style name, and a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a heavier number.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Merge all twenty two records into one press file with one person per page, then render proofs at true print resolution and look at the pages themselves rather than at the count.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to row count proves the run assembled, not that a record is complete. The roster is the only place where the longest strings live and the artwork is the only place they can be judged.
trajectory.produces: A press file for the printer plus proofs at trim resolution, inspected page by page.

trajectory.action: Produce the separate single passes, one per person, and name each file to the roster on download.
trajectory.judgement: Multi record raster output cannot be named by its position in the returned list, so identity has to come from a route that guarantees it rather than from the order the addresses arrive in.
trajectory.produces: Twenty two single passes, each named to the person it carries.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the field and dusk atmosphere frame, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the festival target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns nothing, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained file carrying three A2 poster roots, each root declaring its own canvas, with every photograph inlined as embedded image data and the mark placed as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored top and left.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized wrapper anchored from the right throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a multi root set. The design work is whether the three are genuinely three directions.
trajectory.produces: An export ready source file for the poster series, retained as the durable half of the deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and audit the returned per canvas markup for the other two.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable poster document, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Author and export the announcement set as one document carrying the square, the tall and the four by five at their own canvas sizes, plus the site plan drawn as inline SVG and the basis page recording colours, type and mark.
trajectory.judgement: Mixed canvas sizes in one document is the whole reason this set can be one working file. The site plan is vector work, so it is drawn rather than photographed, and the legend is where the mark reproduces smallest.
trajectory.produces: A native editable announcement and reference document with the site plan as real editable vector.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success code, and vector artwork is not boardable so the mark belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that next year's freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover note.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What last year's pass actually becomes once it is a working document, and whether a mapping the tools blessed actually landed. The printed page shows five clearly separated blocks; the converted document can expose them as a single continuous text flow with no addressable per field frames, and the photo box that reads as a picture frame on paper can convert as drawn artwork with no graphic frame at all, which removes the per performer headshot binding the roster's filename column was written for. On top of that, the readout used to compute the mapping can silently omit a low contrast run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run. The validator answers VALID with no warnings and the prepare step answers completed successfully, and only a placeholder inventory taken back out of the document reveals that some fields never landed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it because the granularity of a converted PDF is a property of the source artwork and is not exposed until the conversion has been run and the document read back. Nothing in the brief, the file listing or the printed page states any of it: the client believes the pass is five fields and a photo box, which is what it looks like. The response is not a re run of the same chain, it is a different mapping strategy entirely, offsets computed inside one story against a reconstructed text, plus a decision about what to do with a headshot that now has nowhere to go.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from a reconstructed story text rather than the readout, re prepare the template, re verify the placeholder inventory field by field, and re plan the headshot: either carry it as part of the delivered artwork by another route or tell the client plainly that this year's pass cannot carry a photo from this source.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A twenty two page run that assembles cleanly and prints with several fields blank or still carrying last year's artwork text, discovered by a gate steward on the first morning of a festival that has already been laminated.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every record survives the frame it landed in. The pass measure is fixed, and a string longer than the measure does not overset visibly and does not raise a warning: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the record looks complete, the run reports success and the page count still equals the row count. Which of the twenty two this happens to is a function of each act's own billing string against the inherited frame width, and no column, no count and no response says which.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it, because the frame width is inherited from artwork the client supplied rather than chosen. Nothing states it either: the brief says the roster is final and lists what each pass must carry, and the acceptance line about nothing truncating is the printer's standing requirement, not a disclosure that a particular act is too long. And the response is not a re merge of the same thing, it is a craft decision per affected record about measure, about how the act line is set, or about what abbreviates without misbilling an act.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every page of the proof at trim rather than the run summary, identify the records that stop short, change the way the act and stage strings are set for the whole run so one rule covers all twenty two, then re merge, re render and re read.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Laminates printed and heat sealed with an act billed as half its own name and a performer cleared for stages the pass does not show, on the one artefact that cannot be corrected after it is made.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still holds where it is smallest. The trace off the painted banner comes back clean, complete and convincing at canvas size, and it sits well at poster scale. At the size it actually reproduces in the announcement set corner lockup and in the site plan legend, over the dark ground both of those sit on, the lantern's window panes and the counters inside the type ring can close and fill in, and the hand painted rule can thicken into the ring. Nothing reports it, because the trace succeeded, the vector is valid and the placement is correct.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the reproduction size and the ground only exist once the canvases are composed, and no measurement is available anywhere in the connector to predict it. Nothing states it: the brief asks for the mark back as artwork for the posters, the announcement set and the programme, and never asks how small it can go. The response is not a re export, it is a different raster preparation upstream, a selection weighted to the paint body rather than to its edges, or a plate filled and traced at a different polarity, producing a second mark drawn for small use.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Prepare and trace a small use variant of the mark from the banner by a different route, judge it at true reproduction size on the actual dark ground rather than on canvas, re place it in the announcement set and the legend, re export, and record the two variants and their intended sizes in the basis page and the note.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An announcement set going out on the on sale morning to four thousand ticket buyers with the festival's mark reduced to a dark blob in the corner, and a programme legend where the lantern has no windows.

deliverables.name: Lanternwood 2027 performer laminate run
deliverables.spec: Twenty two laminates built off last year's printed artwork: one press file the printer can run with one person per page and page count equal to roster count, plus twenty two separate single passes named to the roster, plus proofs at true print resolution sized to the pass trim. Every field carries that person's own value, nothing is inherited from last year's text, no record truncates at trim, and the role colour coding is one reconciled scheme.

deliverables.name: Lanternwood headliner poster series, three A2 directions
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying three A2 roots, each keeping its own canvas, presented as three genuinely different directions for the festival's two directors to choose between rather than one layout in three colourways. Live editable text in one licensed type system, the recovered mark as real vector shapes, every photograph carried as embedded image data, delivered with the self contained source file it was authored from.

deliverables.name: Lineup announcement set, site plan and festival basis page
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying the square, the tall and the four by five announcement canvases at their own sizes, the site plan redrawn from the pencil scan as real editable vector with a legend, and a basis page recording the palette, the type system by role and the mark with its intended sizes. Contractual sponsor lines present and unreworded on every canvas that carries them.

deliverables.name: Lanternwood house photography set
deliverables.spec: The fourteen archive frames brought to one festival target, one white point, one black point, one crop logic, with a per frame parameter log and a line on why any frame differs from its neighbours, plus one licensed camera scale field frame graded into the same world. Frames that cannot be brought to the set are named. The reconciliation of frames against approved billing is delivered with the set, including which billed act the archive does not cover.

deliverables.name: Recovered Lanternwood mark
deliverables.spec: The lantern and type ring lockup recovered from a photograph of a painted banner as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, delivered as a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, holding its window panes and its ring counters at the size it actually reproduces and over the festival's darkest ground.

deliverables.name: Handover note and directors' selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording the pass template's real structure and what it can and cannot carry, the per record decisions taken to keep every laminate whole, the per photograph parameters, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the mark's two variants and their intended sizes, and anything that could not be produced. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the graded selects and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count of the delivered press file and read each page's name field against the roster.

verifiers_auto.text: Twenty two separate single passes exist, each named to a roster person, and each one's content matches its filename.
verifiers_auto.how: List the delivered per record files and read the name field on each against its own filename.

verifiers_auto.text: Every mapped field placeholder is present in the prepared template's story, with none silently dropped.
verifiers_auto.how: Export the prepared template's interchange form and grep the stories for each expected field token.

verifiers_auto.text: Proofs are at true print resolution at the pass trim, not a screen scale preview.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel dimensions and embedded density of the delivered proofs against the pass trim size.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered mark's SVG carries a viewBox and no full canvas opaque background path at index zero.

verifiers_auto.text: The poster export returned three roots and the announcement export returned its canvases, each keeping its own declared size.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in both exports carries a resolved licensed face rather than a fallback default, and the contractual sponsor lines appear unaltered.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup against the families the kit call returned, and string match the sponsor lines against the supplied copy.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered raster exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop record in the run carries an enlargement entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare each delivered file's dimensions against its source per the manifest and diff the captured tradeoff records against the note's resize table.

verifiers_human.text: Every laminate is whole at trim: no act, role or stage list stops short of its own string.
verifiers_human.how: Read all twenty two proof pages at trim against the roster, line by line, rather than reading the run summary.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a record per page variable data run and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout at all.
Whether to trust the mapping readout or to reconstruct the template's true story text before computing a single offset.
What to do about a headshot column written for a photo box that turns out not to be a photo box.
How the act and stage strings are set across the whole run so that one rule keeps all twenty two records whole, rather than patching the records that happen to fail.
How far to push the two into the sun frames before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
Whether fourteen archive frames covers a three headliner billing, and how to say so when it does not.

Selection wording on the painted banner: naming the substrate takes the canvas, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries which canvas, judged at reproduction size on the actual ground rather than at canvas size.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a hundred and forty five dollar weekend ticket and a discovery led crowd, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the three poster directions differ in the ways a director can actually choose between, or only in colour.
How much of the field the announcement set gives to the discovery stages, since the tiering is the whole commercial argument of the festival.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome picture of a folk festival poster. IDENTITY: the mark has to be RECOVERED off a photograph of the actual painted banner that has hung over the main stage since 2022, because a regenerated lantern is a different festival's logo, and the photography has to be of the acts who are actually billed. SPEC: twenty two laminates, one person per page, each carrying that person's own name, act, role, stages and days, printed at trim by a printer who cannot fix a truncated act name afterwards, plus separate single files named to the roster. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked for any of it. EDITABILITY: the client says outright that acts will move through the winter and they will be changing the announcement set themselves, so the deliverable is defined by being a document they can open and retype. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: what the converted pass actually contains, whether the mapping the validator blessed actually landed, whether this record survived its frame, whether the mark holds at the size it reproduces.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous, with a bare press PDF reverse engineered into a live merge template end to end. One record per page is confirmed for PDF output (page count equals row count), per record files are confirmed in correct order via createSeparateFiles and via a per record range loop, and true print resolution is confirmed through document_render_layout rather than through the merge tool, whose own resolution parameter is silently ignored. The first checkpoint rests on two documented findings rather than assumptions: frame granularity from a PDF is not under the author's control and a continuous flow converted to exactly ONE text frame with ZERO graphic frames, and the mapping readout is LOSSY, dropping a run while keeping its line break so that every later offset is short while the validator still answers VALID and prepare still answers completed successfully (three of five mappings landed in the audit). The headshot column is deliberately unbindable because a converted PDF only exposes image frames when the source PDF carried placed images. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, fill_area and vectorize are verified across 27 live calls, and the mark recovery rests on the verified substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the polarity trap before tracing, the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero. EXPRESS: multi root export and mixed canvas sizes in one document are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load, with the case sensitivity and non standard numeric weight traps live. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real camera scale JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of twelve placements per call and a partial success reported as a success code. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed claim off a converted PDF, no pdfPreset, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above twenty.
